w: Because of illness, Swamishri was feeling physically weak. All day long he spent resting, reading letters and in important meetings
At 10.35am, Swamishri inaugurated and sanctified the BAPS organized Pramukh Swami Hospital and Research Center.
A Women's Day program was held in the afternoon.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha yagna in which 770 devotees performed the rituals in the 82 yagna kunds.
At 5.15 p.m., a felicitation assembly was held to honor all those who had contributed for the mandir project. (For details see News report)
After his morning puja, Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs for the villages of Karoli and Malataj.
Swamishri presided over and blessed the 3rd Annual Day Celebration of Pramukh Swami Computer Institute.

Because Swamishri had pain in his calf and neck, he was being given physiotherapy. Making good use of the time during physiotherapy, Swamishri began reading the book 'Li. Shastri Yagnapurushdas'. Not for a day or so, but for weeks this routine went on. In about an hour and a half Swamishri would read some fifty pages with full concentration. Once he sat on a seat and started reading, he would not change position at all, and would be so absorbed in the book that even after the therapy was over his eyes would not leave it! If the attendants did not say, "It is finished now," the reading would go on! He would keep reading until that episode or chapter was complete! At times, seeing Swamishri so absorbed, everyone felt that Swamishri was reading the book as if Guruhari Shastriji Maharaj himself were seated before him!
This devotion of Swamishri to reading left a lasting mark on everyone's heart.
During the meetings an elderly man came. He could not sleep at night. He kept imagining that 20 or 25 people were making a racket and would not let him sleep, as if someone had entered him!
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "Only Swaminarayan has entered us; no one else has entered at all. Swaminarayan is seated in the soul, so do bhajan peacefully and sleep will come."
